question: What is the primary goal of identifying clinical risks in a maternity ward?

options.A: To reduce the cost of buying hospital drugs
options.B: To prevent accidental harm to mothers and babies
options.C: To punish staff who make mistakes on duty
options.D: To make patients stay longer in the hospital

explanation: Identifying clinical risks allows healthcare workers to spot dangers early so they can stop accidents before they happen to patients. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why is poor hand hygiene considered a major clinical risk in a hospital?

options.A: It causes patients to slip and fall on wet floors
options.C: It leads to severe medication administration errors
options.D: It slows down the speed of patient shift handovers

explanation: Germs pass easily from one patient to another on unwashed hands, spreading dangerous infections across the ward. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which group of postpartum mothers is most at risk of experiencing a sudden fall?

options.A: Mothers who walked around easily throughout their entire pregnancy
options.B: Mothers recovering from regional anesthesia and blood loss
options.C: Mothers whose babies were discharged home ahead of schedule
options.D: Mothers who refuse to eat hospital food after delivery

explanation: Anesthesia and blood loss make mothers dizzy and weak, greatly increasing their chances of falling when they try to stand up. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h2)

question: What should a midwife do first when a newly delivered mother wants to walk to the bathroom for the very first time?

options.A: Lock the bathroom door from the outside for safety
options.B: Accompany and physically support her during the walk
options.C: Leave the room so she can maintain her personal privacy
options.D: Tell her to run quickly so she finishes before getting tired

explanation: Being right there to support a weak mother prevents sudden dizziness from turning into a dangerous fall. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the correct action to take with a used injection needle to prevent injury?

options.A: Recap the needle tightly using both hands before disposal
options.B: Leave it on the bedside tray until the end of the shift
options.C: Drop it immediately into a puncture-resistant safety box
options.D: Break the needle off the syringe using bare fingers

explanation: Putting needles straight into a safety box without recapping stops accidental needle-stick injuries to staff. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why must a blood pressure cuff be wiped down between different patients?

options.A: To stop the transfer of harmful bacteria from person to person
options.B: To prevent the rubber tubing from becoming stiff and cracking
options.C: To keep the fabric looking clean and smelling fresh for visitors
options.D: To make sure the digital screen displays accurate blood pressure

explanation: Wiping shared equipment kills lingering germs, preventing cross-contamination across different patients in the ward. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h3)

question: How many patient identifiers should a midwife check before giving any medication?

options.A: Only one identifier to save time
options.D: No identifiers if the bed is known

explanation: Using two identifiers like name and hospital number ensures the right drug goes to the right person. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h4)

question: What should a midwife do when a drug dosage order written in a case note looks unclear?

options.A: Guess the correct amount based on the patient's body weight
options.B: Ask another junior student to make the final decision
options.C: Skip giving that specific dose for the day entirely
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the drug

explanation: Never guess an unclear order because doing so can easily cause a severe medication overdose or error. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why must heavy oxygen cylinders be chained securely to a wall or heavy trolley?

options.A: To stop patients from stealing them for home medical use
options.B: To prevent them from falling over and becoming dangerous projectiles
options.C: To keep the floor space completely open for nursing wheel stretchers
options.D: To ensure they remain close to electrical sockets at all times

explanation: Unsecured oxygen cylinders are heavy and can cause major injuries or explosions if knocked over. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT recommended when dealing with a wet hospital floor?

options.A: Place a bright caution sign near the wet area immediately
options.B: Inform housekeeping staff to ensure thorough drying
options.C: Leave the floor wet with no warning signs so people run slowly
options.D: Mop up the spilled liquid as quickly as possible

explanation: Failing to warn people about a wet floor invites slip and fall accidents, which violates basic safety rules. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h5)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the beginning of the SBAR communication tool?
explanation: SBAR starts with Situation, helping the nurse quickly state what is currently happening with the patient. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h6)

question: How should a midwife confirm a patient's identity before starting an IV infusion?

options.A: Check the patient chart resting on the nurse's station desk
options.B: Call out the patient's first name and see if anyone answers
options.C: Look at the bed number painted on the frame of the hospital bed
options.D: Ask the patient to state their full name and check their ID band

explanation: Combining active verbal questioning with checking the physical ID band prevents dangerous mix-ups in patient identity. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of writing an incident report after a near-miss occurs?

options.A: To gather evidence that proves which staff member was lazy
options.B: To increase the hospital fees charged to the patient
options.C: To make sure the nurse involved gets suspended from work
options.D: To learn from system flaws and improve future patient safety

explanation: Incident reports help hospitals spot weak spots in their systems so they can fix them before real harm happens. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h7)

question: What best describes a 'near-miss' event in a maternity ward?

options.A: An error occurred, but it was caught just in time before harming the patient
options.B: A doctor successfully performed an emergency cesarean section
options.C: A visitor slipped on the stairs outside the main maternity entrance
options.D: A patient experienced severe complications because treatment was delayed

explanation: A near-miss is a close call where a mistake happened, but quick intervention stopped it from reaching the patient. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h7)
